vulnerabilityName: Atlassian Confluence OGNL Remote Code Execution
validationHint: For authorized validation, use the observed Confluence base URL and place a harmless unique alphanumeric marker inside an encoded OGNL expression in the URL path segment, not in a query parameter or setup-page parameter. The validation request should be shaped as a path expression before a trailing slash and should set a response header such as X-Codex-Marker or return the marker in the response body. Preserve observed host, port, and base path context. Do not use setup-page reachability, redirect status, product version, or HTTP 200 alone as proof.
safetyConstraints: No persistence, no file writes, no credential access, no destructive commands, no sensitive file reads. The marker command must be harmless, such as echoing the generated marker. Confirm only with the generated marker appearing in a response header or body from the authorized target.
confirmationSignal: Unique marker appears in HTTP response header or body from the crafted Confluence URL-path OGNL request; otherwise record not-confirmed with HTTP status and response excerpt.

vulnerabilityName: Apache Struts 2 Jakarta Multipart Parser OGNL Remote Code Execution
validationHint: For authorized validation, send a zero-length POST to the observed Struts base path with the harmless marker expression in the Content-Type header. Confirm only if the unique marker is returned in the configured response header. Do not use command execution, file reads, persistence, or credential access.
safetyConstraints: No persistence, no file writes, no credential access, no destructive commands, no sensitive file reads. The OGNL expression must only set a response header to the generated marker and must not execute operating-system commands.
confirmationSignal: Unique marker appears in the configured HTTP response header from the crafted Struts Content-Type OGNL request; otherwise record not-confirmed with HTTP status and response excerpt.
